title: = I39a: the Go derivation extracted (ParseBatch as an extracted consumer: I18's skeleton document of node/derivation plus the SSA of ParseBatch's closure, its environment named) and the product machine joining the Solidity commit (the adopted Rollup document's commitBatch, evaluator-level) with Go derivation through the derivation's own calldata join and the committed header as the next parent (the cycle), its consumer half refined against a Go replay of the real BatchInfo.ParseBatch on 169 batches; no laws

predictions.claim: The consumer is extracted as read (D1-D4): spec/M3/facts/morph_derivation.extracted.json, less its consumer key, is I18's spec/M2/facts/morph_derivation.go.extracted.json (the same frontend, config and package set); its consumer section's closure is the 14 functions of thresholds.closure (ParseBatch, the BlockContext decoder and node/types' DecodeBlockContext, the transaction queue's enqueue and dequeue and constructor, encodeTransactions, the five BatchHeaderBytes methods it reaches (BatchIndex, TotalL1MessagePopped, Version, LastBlockNumber, validate), RetrieveBlobBytes and the zstd wrapper DecompressBatchBytes); its environment is exactly the 13 callees of thresholds.environment with their kinds (9 standard-library natives: fmt.Errorf, errors.New, bytes.NewReader, encoding/binary.Read, the big-endian Uint16 and Uint64, math/big's NewInt, SetBytes and Cmp; the oracles DecompressMorphDABatch and DecodeTxsFromBytes; Transactions.Len as a slice length; Transaction.MarshalBinary as an encoding); no callee, global or instruction is unaccounted; the instrument's walk over the section gives the same closure and environment. Derivation: reading the sources at the head: every static call of those bodies, with the sidecar's boundary at DecodeTxsFromBytes and the cgo decompressor; the bodies use structs, pointers, slices, append, copy, make, interfaces for fmt's and binary.Read's arguments and two counted loops, all ops the interpreter evaluates; the globals they read are common/batch's three error variables (assigned by errors.New in a package initializer) and binary.BigEndian.

The join is as read (J1): gen/M3/derivation/product.json's join rows are the seven of thresholds.join, which the instrument recomputes from the document's join function and the Rollup document's commitBatch parameter: each BatchDataInput member, through the Go field its first letter capitalized names (go-ethereum's ABI decoder fills modernBatchDataInput by those names), lands in the RPCRollupBatch field unpackModernRollupCall's literal stores it into: version, parentBatchHeader, lastBlockNumber, numL1Messages, prevStateRoot and postStateRoot under their own names, withdrawalRoot as WithdrawRoot. Derivation: reading unpackModernRollupCall (the composite literal at derivation.go:700-708); no member is dropped by the join.

The consumer's read set (D5): ParseBatch reads exactly BlockContexts, LastBlockNumber, ParentBatchHeader, PostStateRoot, Sidecar (and Sidecar.Blobs), Version and WithdrawRoot of its batch, and never reads NumL1Messages, PrevStateRoot, Hash, CurrentSequencerSetBytes or Signatures (thresholds.reads, thresholds.unread; together they are every field of RPCRollupBatch). Derivation: reading batch_info.go:87-248. The committed L1-message count reaches the derived batch (P2) and is then discarded: F11's L1-count observation, as an extraction fact; I39 states its law.

The product machine commits and closes the cycle (J2, J3, K1-K5): on the 8 product traces (20 commits) every planned commit is ok on the adopted Rollup document from I80's deployment record under the declared environment, with batch index k for the k-th commit; each committed header (the argument of the keccak256 written to committedBatches) hashes to the word written; each next commit's parent is that header (the first's is I20's genesis); and the derivation of each committed batch agrees with the real ParseBatch and is ok with batchIndex the committed index for versions 1 and 2, and fails with "invalid batch: zero block count" for version 0 (thresholds.product_v0_error). Derivation: the commits follow I20's harness rule (parent hash, index, previous state root, non-zero roots, an active submitter, an empty queue so no L1-message delay); a modern commit carries no calldata contexts, so a version 0 batch has no block count (batch_info.go:114-198), while versions 1 and 2 count blocks from the parent's last block number, which the Solidity header stores.

The consumer refines the real ParseBatch (G1-G5, C4-C5): on all 169 cases (thresholds.cases: 29 planted, 120 random, 20 product) the interpreter of the document's consumer SSA, its environment answered by Go's standard-library semantics and by the real library's decompressor and transaction decoder, agrees with the Go replay of the real BatchInfo.ParseBatch in status, error text, panic text and the whole receiver's dump: 0 disagreements, 0 unsupported; steps.json recounts to refinement.json and its real sides are the replay report's. Derivation: the closure's ops have exact Go semantics in the interpreter; the texts come from the same format strings and runtime messages; the environment is the real library's. This is the least certain prediction: one formatting verb, one nil-versus-empty slice or one runtime text the interpreter gets wrong misses it.

The corpus reaches every live return (C4-C5): among the agreeing cases, each of ParseBatch's 15 live returns (thresholds.sites.reached: batch_info.go:89, 94, 118, 124, 138, 147, 158, 171, 175, 186, 198, 203, 229, 235 and the ok return at 247) ends at least one case; its 5 dead returns (98, 131, 142, 153, 212) end none; and at least one case panics with "runtime error: index out of range [126976] with length 126976" (O4's site in RetrieveBlobBytes, reached through derivation). Derivation: reading ParseBatch: 98 and 131 re-check a header that BatchIndex has already validated, 153 asks a validated version-1-or-later parent for its last block number, and 142 and 212 decode exactly 60 bytes, which DecodeBlockContext always accepts; the planted cases were chosen for the other returns.
